title: Magellan-Elcano circumnavigation
summary: Between 1519 and 1522, an expedition commissioned by the Spanish crown and initially led by Ferdinand Magellan achieved the first recorded circumnavigation of the globe. After navigating a strait into the Pacific Ocean, Magellan was killed in the Philippines in 1521; Basque navigator Juan Sebastián Elcano subsequently brought the sole surviving ship, the Victoria, back to Spain across the Indian Ocean, empirically proving the Earth's circumference and interconnected marine routes.

uncertainty.note: Fleet sailed downriver from Seville on 10 August 1519 and departed Sanlúcar de Barrameda into the open Atlantic on 20 September 1519; Victoria returned to Sanlúcar on 6 September 1522.

as_recorded.value: Saturday the 6th of September of the year 1522, we entered the bay of San Lucar

where.historical_name: Sanlúcar de Barrameda, Kingdom of Seville, Crown of Castile

importance.justification: Completed the first global circumnavigation, empirically demonstrating Earth's spherical geometry and interconnected ocean systems.

related.because: Columbus's voyage established the Spanish transatlantic crossing that Magellan sought to extend westward to the Spice Islands.

beats.caption: Magellan's fleet of five ships departs Spain seeking a westward passage to the Spice Islands.
The Victoria returns to Sanlúcar de Barrameda under Elcano, completing the first global circumnavigation.
